messages:
Claire (Brightline SI): P0: Customer go-live tomorrow 09:00 PT. Private deploy failing: app nodes can't resolve internal-service.* via private DNS across peering; also KMS key access from HSM in customer account failing with AccessDenied. Need arch review + short-term workaround. @Alex R @Maya L :rotating_light:
Alex R: On it. Can you paste VPC IDs, peering ID, and the failing pod logs? Also are you using Redwood Private (managed control plane) or Dedicated?
Claire (Brightline SI): VPCs: vpc-0a1b2c3d / vpc-0f9e8d7c, peering pcx-04aa55, using Redwood Private (managed control plane). Pod log: `dial tcp: lookup internal-service on 169.254.169.253:53: no such host`
Maya L: That DNS addr looks like our stub resolver — maybe coreDNS forwarding not set for peered CIDR. Check route tables + security groups for DNS port 53 UDP/TCP. Also KMS error? paste the HSM log snippet.
Claire (Brightline SI): HSM logs: `AccessDeniedException: Caller is not authorized to use the key` when calling `Encrypt` from HSM (customer account A -> key in account B). We had cross-account grant configured but customer uses role under different external ID — could be missing key policy stmt.
Samir: If cross-account grants are flaky, can we add a short-term fallback: create a customer-scoped KMS key in their account and update backend to use that via env var? Might be faster than key policy edits.
Alex R: Agree we can fallback. But need ops sign-off because it's cryptographic boundary change. @Evan can you weigh in? Also we should open a joint call with Brightline + infra ops. Claire, can you share runbook link and propose 30-min window?
Evan: I can be on call. Quick checks: 1) `kubectl exec` into a pod and `dig internal-service @10.100.0.2 +short` 2) confirm coreDNS forwarding config in `Corefile` 3) show KMS policy blob. If you DM the policy I can scan.
Claire (Brightline SI): Running dig now... `dig internal-service @10.100.0.2 +short` -> no output. Corefile shows `forward . 169.254.169.253` (that's our stub).
Maya L: That mismatch explains it — peering needs conditional forwarding or we need to run dnsmasq on the peered subnets. Short-term: add a route to send 169.254.169.253 traffic to the peering? Not ideal. Better: update CoreDNS forwarders to include the partner resolver IP (10.200.0.11) — can you test with `dig @10.200.0.11`?
Claire (Brightline SI): Test: `dig internal-service @10.200.0.11 +short` -> returns 10.1.5.12. So partner resolver works. I'll request partner to allow queries from our control plane subnet (they have an allowlist).
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0123 — Brightline private DNS + KMS (assigned to eng-infra). Priorities: P0, SLA: 4h.
Samir: For KMS, Claire please attach the error trace and the principal ARN. We can add a key policy statement granting `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Brightline-HSM` permission to `Encrypt`/`Decrypt` for the duration of go-live.
Claire (Brightline SI): Attached policy and principal in DM. I'll coordinate call for 30 min at 21:00 UTC. Can we also prepare an A/B failover plan to use the customer-local KMS if policy change is blocked?
Alex R: :thumbsup: I'll draft the rollback/fallback steps and a one-liner for the PM to communicate to customer. Meeting invite sent to Brightline, Evan, Maya, Samir.
Claire (Brightline SI): Thanks everyone — going to start on the CoreDNS change request and confirm partner allowlist. I'll update in this thread after call.
